clue.text: After training all but wild hybrid rook becomes a flyer

indicators.note: training licks something into a new shape, so the letters that follow are rearranged
all but means every letter except one, here the last of wild

parts.note: R is the chess abbreviation for rook

explanation.surface: A wild hybrid bird, once trained, becomes a good flyer: a falconer's success story.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests falconry, but the flyer is a machine: 'all but' cuts the last letter from the word wild, and 'After training' rearranges the pooled letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Whirlybird is a slang name for a helicopter, an aircraft and so a flyer.

clue.text: Hit for pop duo

definitions.meaning: a hit or blow, a forceful strike
the 1980s British pop pair of George Michael and Andrew Ridgeley

explanation.surface: A hit record for a pop duo.
explanation.definitionFit: Wham is both an exclamation-turned-noun for a heavy blow and the name of the duo Wham!

clue.text: Initially injection neutralises salt content of pulp in hormone

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letters of the next three words
the content of a word is what lies inside it, its middle letters

explanation.surface: An injection that cancels out the salt in pulp, as if describing a lab treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initially' covers injection, neutralises and salt, giving INS; 'content of' takes UL from pulp.
explanation.definitionFit: Insulin is the pancreatic hormone regulating blood sugar, often given by injection.

clue.text: Jock's chimney basically said to produce light

parts.note: lum is the Scottish word for a chimney; Jock is a Scotsman

indicators.note: said tells us to use the spoken form of the phrase meaning basically

parts.note: basically means in essence

explanation.surface: A Scotsman's chimney, essentially, gives off light.
explanation.walkthrough: Jock is crossword shorthand for a Scot, so 'Jock's' signals a Scottish word.
explanation.definitionFit: Luminescence is the glow given off by a substance without heat, a form of light.

clue.text: Male deer said to intimidate

parts.note: a bull is a male of several animals, including deer such as elk

indicators.note: said marks a word to be taken by its pronunciation

parts.note: does are female deer

explanation.surface: A stag is said to frighten others off.
explanation.definitionFit: To bulldoze someone is to force or bully them into submission.

clue.text: Émigré's unorthodox course of treatment

indicators.note: unorthodox means irregular, so the letters are put out of their usual order

parts.note: the letters of émigré with its accents dropped; the possessive 's adds no letter

explanation.surface: An exile is following an unusual medical regimen.
explanation.definitionFit: A regime can mean a prescribed programme of diet or therapy, a regimen.

clue.text: Penniless rascal's a cheat

indicators.note: penniless means without a penny, abbreviated P, so that letter is removed

parts.note: a scamp is a rascal

explanation.surface: A broke rogue is a swindler.
explanation.definitionFit: A scam is a swindle or fraud, so a cheat in the noun sense.

clue.text: Chats about fare at first entering taxis

indicators.note: entering means the following letters go inside the word for taxis

parts.note: cabs are taxis
on means about, concerning

indicators.note: at first takes the opening letter of fare

explanation.surface: Cabbies talk about the fare as passengers get in.
explanation.definitionFit: Confabs are informal conversations, short for confabulations.

clue.text: Lehar work rewrite worried my wife

indicators.note: a rewrite produces a new version, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A rewrite of a Lehár operetta has upset the speaker's spouse.
explanation.definitionFit: The Merry Widow is Franz Lehár's best-known operetta.

clue.text: Fool without a smidgin of sense gambles away European collection

parts.note: an ass is a fool

indicators.note: away suggests letters gone astray, so they are rearranged
without means the letter named is left out
a smidgin is a tiny bit, here just the first letter of sense

explanation.surface: A senseless fool gambles away a European collection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes S from GAMBLES, leaving GAMBLE, which 'away' rearranges to EMBLAG.
explanation.definitionFit: An assemblage is a gathering or collection of things or people.

clue.text: John Kerr regularly proves to be expert

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the name

explanation.surface: John Kerr proves himself an expert, a sporting compliment.
explanation.definitionFit: A oner is British slang for someone outstanding at something, an expert.

clue.text: Player is into arranging following agreement

indicators.note: following places the rearranged letters after the word for agreement

parts.note: accord means agreement

indicators.note: arranging means putting the letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A musician gets into arranging once a deal is signed.
explanation.definitionFit: An accordionist plays the accordion, so a player of an instrument.

clue.text: Self-willed, heartless but showing style

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letter is removed

parts.note: elvan is a variant of elvish, meaning mischievous or self-willed

explanation.surface: A wilful, cold person who nonetheless has panache.
explanation.walkthrough: The five-letter word is an old spelling found in Chambers; the clue relies on that dictionary.
explanation.definitionFit: Elan means flair, dash or panache, which is style.

clue.text: Protest about risqué form of government

parts.note: a demo is a protest march
C stands for circa, about
racy means risqué

explanation.surface: A protest over a saucy style of rule.
explanation.definitionFit: Democracy is government by the people, a type of political system.

clue.text: He injects new petty officer being nursed by captain

indicators.note: being nursed means being held inside, here by the word for captain

parts.note: a skipper is a captain
PO is the naval abbreviation for petty officer

explanation.surface: A sailor gets a jab while being looked after by the ship's master.
explanation.definitionFit: A skin-popper is slang for a drug user who injects under the skin.

clue.text: Like Henry VIIIth's bed?

parts.note: the monarch's bed belongs to a king, and he was famously huge, so it is large in two senses

explanation.surface: A question about the Tudor monarch's furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: The term describes an extra-large bed, and a monarch's bed is a royal one.

clue.text: Tree's fine after black wood's tips cut off

indicators.note: after places the word for fine at the end
removing the tips takes away the first and last letters of the wood

parts.note: ebony is a black wood; the 's adds an S
AI, i.e. A1, means first-rate or fine

explanation.surface: A tree is fine once the ends of its dark branches are pruned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tips cut off' strips E and Y from EBONY, leaving BON, plus S from the possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: A bonsai is a miniature potted tree, kept small by pruning.

clue.text: Look round special space at college and relax

parts.note: lo is an old word for look
O is round in shape
an en is a printer's space
up means in residence at university

explanation.surface: Look around a special place at college and chill out.
explanation.definitionFit: To loosen up is to become less tense, to unwind.

clue.text: Posh man, short of money, returns water in disgust

indicators.note: returns means the remaining letters are read backwards

parts.note: U means upper class or posh

indicators.note: short of means lacking, so one letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written
the sea is water

explanation.surface: A toff who has lost his money goes back to sea in disgust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short of' takes M from UMAN, leaving UAN; 'returns' turns that into NAU.
explanation.definitionFit: Nausea is sickness and, figuratively, strong revulsion or loathing.

clue.text: It's acceptable. Start to punish insolence openly

parts.note: U means socially acceptable, upper-class usage

indicators.note: start to means the first letter of punish

parts.note: front means cheek or insolence

explanation.surface: A teacher declares it fine to begin punishing cheek in public.
explanation.definitionFit: Up front means candidly, without concealment, so frankly and openly.

clue.text: Dubious place for cranky old boiler with no current

indicators.note: cranky means eccentric or out of order, so the letters are rearranged
with no means the named letter is taken out

parts.note: I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: An unreliable old boiler without power sits in a doubtful spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no' removes I from BOILER, leaving BOLER; 'cranky' mixes OLD with BOLER.
explanation.definitionFit: A bordello is a brothel, a disreputable establishment.

clue.text: Young English king, with time, exhibits a measure of 3

parts.note: a lamb is a young sheep
R stands for rex, king

explanation.surface: A young English king displays something, with time.
explanation.walkthrough: 3 points to 3-down, glowing light; this answer is a unit of its brightness.
explanation.definitionFit: A lambert is an old unit of luminance, a measure of emitted light.

clue.text: One after the other short sounds from flute are exquisite

indicators.note: one after the other means the shortened word appears twice in a row
short means the last letter is cut

parts.note: toot is the sound a flute makes

explanation.surface: Brief successive flute notes are delicate.
explanation.definitionFit: Too-too is a dated affected term for excessively refined, precious or exquisite.

clue.text: Officer in charge signed debt slips like a Jobsworth

parts.note: OFF is an abbreviation for officer
IOUs are signed notes acknowledging debts

explanation.surface: An officer in charge has signed IOUs, typical of a pettifogging official.
explanation.walkthrough: A Jobsworth is British slang for a petty official who insists on rules ('it's more than my job's worth').
explanation.definitionFit: Officious means self-importantly interfering, just the manner of a petty rule-bound official.

clue.text: Salamanders on old railway line

parts.note: LMS was the London, Midland and Scottish Railway

explanation.surface: Amphibians crossing an old track.
explanation.definitionFit: Olms are blind cave salamanders of southern Europe.

clue.text: Former despot, initially the supreme authority over Russia, banned America's participation

indicators.note: over places the first part above the next in this down entry
initially takes the first letter of each of the next three words
banned means the named letters are excluded

parts.note: RUS is the international vehicle code for Russia
the US, America, as a participant

explanation.surface: A deposed autocrat, supreme ruler of Russia, kept American involvement out.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsar was a Russian emperor, an absolute ruler of the past.

clue.text: Support for party leader

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of

indicators.note: leader takes the first letter of party

explanation.surface: Backing for the head of a political party.
explanation.definitionFit: A prop is something that holds up or supports another thing.

clue.text: Being tight, hiccupping, I start to sing soprano in gents

indicators.note: hiccupping disrupts the flow, so the letters are jumbled
start to takes the first letter of sing

explanation.surface: A man with hiccups starts singing soprano in the men's toilets.
explanation.walkthrough: Gents is British for a men's public lavatory.
explanation.definitionFit: Stinginess is meanness with money, and tight is slang for mean.

clue.text: Appropriate sounding liturgy

indicators.note: sounding asks for a word with the same pronunciation

parts.note: right means appropriate or proper

explanation.surface: A fitting-sounding church service.
explanation.definitionFit: A rite is a prescribed religious ceremony, the form of a service.

clue.text: Rival school's tie twisted round bunk

parts.note: a comp is a comprehensive school; the 's is a link

indicators.note: twisted means the letters of tie are rearranged
round means turned about, so the word for bunk is read backwards

parts.note: rot means bunk, nonsense

explanation.surface: A rival school's tie is wrapped around a bed.
explanation.walkthrough: A comp is a British state comprehensive school. 'twisted' rearranges the three letters of tie, and 'round' turns the word for bunk backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A competitor is an opponent or rival in a contest.
